stories.title: Bally’s Lands $560M Loan From WhiteHawk for Bronx Casino Development
stories.excerpt: Gambling and entertainment giant Bally’s has landed a $560 million debt package from WhiteHawk Capital Partners to fund its casino development in the Bronx, the company announced Monday. The financing from WhiteHawk, a private credit investment manager, will be broken up into a $400 million frontloaded loan and $160 million from delayed-draw term debt with the deal slated to close in the third quarter, according to Bally’s. The loans will fund pre-construction and other expenditures associated with the planned 3 million-square-foot casino development at the Bally’s Golf Links at Ferry Point, which will include a 500-room hotel and a 2,000-person event center. Bally’s acquired the Bronx site — formerly leased as a public golf course to Donald Trump — for $156.6 million from New York City in February, Commercial Observer previously reported. “This important financing allows us to progress the pre-construction planning process so that we are ready to complete the remainder of the capital raise and remain on schedule,” Soo Kim, chairman of the board at Bally’s, said in a statement. “Furthermore, the additional liquidity provides us greater flexibility for other capital opportunities.” Bob Louzan, managing partner at WhiteHawk Capital Partners, said in a statement that the financing “will support the project’s pre-construction work as Bally’s advances its broader financing plan.” Bally’s Bronx casino proposal at 450 Hutchinson River Parkway was one of three gambling projects approved by New York State in December. The other two selected were Resorts World New York City at the former Aqueduct Raceway in Jamaica, Queens, and Hard Rock’s Metropolitan Park next to Citi Field in Flushing, Queens, to be developed in partnership with New York Mets owner Steve Cohen. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Bally's secures $560M from WhiteHawk: $400M upfront + $160M delayed-draw for Bronx casino
3M-sq-ft development includes 500-room hotel, 2,000-seat event center at Ferry Point
Site acquired Feb 2024 for $156.6M; financing closes Q3 2026
stories.summary: Bally's Corporation closed $560 million in debt financing from WhiteHawk Capital Partners to fund pre-construction and development of its 3 million-square-foot Bronx casino project at Ferry Point. The deal includes a $400 million term loan and $160 million delayed-draw component, closing Q3 2026. The project will house a 500-room hotel and 2,000-person event center on land Bally's acquired from NYC for $156.6 million in February 2024.
stories.impact: Major entertainment venue development signals NYC market confidence and catalyzes mixed-use activation in South Bronx. Multifamily developers should monitor secondary residential demand spillover near Ferry Point—the hotel component and event center will drive daytime population concentration, but ancillary residential development (workforce, visitor extensions, neighborhood density) should be underwritten within 0.5–1.5 mile radius as infrastructure and services mature post-opening. Financing close in Q3 2026 suggests construction timeline; neighborhood-serving multifamily could align with phased delivery.

stories.title: Partners Inks Leasing Deal for Houston’s Intercontinental Center
stories.excerpt: Partners Real Estate has been selected as the exclusive leasing agent for Intercontinental Center, a nine-story, 200,250-square-foot Class A office building at 15600 John F. Kennedy Blvd. in Houston. Vince Strake and Brad Beasley of the firm’s Office Agency Leasing practice will lead the assignment. Intercontinental Center sits in the North Houston corridor between the North Belt and George Bush Intercontinental Airport, with access to the rest of the city via U.S. 59, I-45 and the Hardy Toll Road. Building amenities include a conferencing facility, an on-site fitness center, a micro-market, 24-hour courtesy officer coverage, and an attached garage with covered parking for tenants and visitors. This latest win comes on the heels of a continued run of success for Partners’ Office Agency Leasing team in Houston, which most recently includes being named the exclusive leasing agent for TotalEnergies Tower, the 834,000-square foot downtown landmark at 1201 Louisiana, awarded by The Wideman Company in July. The building includes conferencing, fitness, micro-market, and attached parking. Brokers Vince Strake and Brad Beasley lead the assignment.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. Office leasing activity in North Houston near IAH reflects corporate demand but does not signal residential supply or demand shifts. Monitor only if tenant base expands—large employer moves to the corridor could indirectly support multifamily fundamentals, but this is a broker assignment on existing Class A stock, not a demand catalyst.

stories.title: Wu Administration Eyes $100M Development Incentive Program for Stalled Projects
stories.excerpt: Boston Mayor Michelle Wu is proposing a $100-million development incentive program to help jumpstart large residential developments her administration says are stalled by high construction and borrowing costs, the Boston Business Journal reported Monday. The program would start with $31 million for four development projects totaling about 1,400 units, including One Mystic, a 408-unit tower in Charlestown’s Sullivan Square, and a 341-unit building at Allston Yards. These, along with a second Allston project and another in Brighton, fit the Wu administration’s target for larger projects that need only a financial boost to become feasible and start construction. City officials said the projects could be ready to launch construction early next year. The initiative needs approval by the Boston Planning & Development Agency, which is set to consider approval at its next meeting in October. If approved, it would be a significant expansion of developer incentives in the city, reported the Business Journal. bullets: Boston Mayor Wu proposes $100M development incentive program for stalled residential projects
$31M initial tranche targets four projects totaling ~1,400 units (One Mystic 408-unit Charlestown, Allston Yards 341-unit)

stories.summary: Boston Mayor Michelle Wu is proposing a $100 million development incentive program to jumpstart stalled residential projects citing high construction and borrowing costs. The initiative would begin with $31 million for four projects totaling approximately 1,400 units, including One Mystic (408 units) in Charlestown's Sullivan Square and Allston Yards (341 units). The Boston Planning & Development Agency is expected to approve in October, with projects potentially breaking ground early 2025.
stories.impact: Direct supply signal for Greater Boston multifamily market. High construction costs and financing stress have frozen delivery pipeline; Wu's subsidy program (if approved) removes financial feasibility gap and unlocks ~1,400 units of mid-term supply. Developers should model subsidy structures and timeline: $31M for 1,400 units = ~$22k/unit gap-closing capital. This suggests softer underwriting assumptions (lower stabilized rents, extended lease-up) drove original delays. Monitor approval and actual disbursement—if other Boston projects qualify, expect inventory acceleration 2025–2027, pressure on rents in Charlestown, Allston, and Brighton submarkets.

stories.title: Bally’s Secures $560M Financing for Bronx Casino Project
stories.excerpt: Bally’s Corporation said Monday that it secured new financing led by WhiteHawk Capital Partners, LP to fund further development of the Bally’s Bronx project and general corporate purposes. The new financing comprises closing-date term loan commitments in an aggregate principal amount of $400 million and delayed-draw term loan commitments in an aggregate principal amount of $160 million. Proceeds of the loans will be used to fund certain pre-construction costs and expenditures associated with the development of the Bally’s Bronx project, with a portion of the proceeds available to the company for general corporate purposes. The new financing is expected to close in the third quarter of 2026. Bally’s board chairman Soo Kim said, “This important financing allows us to progress the pre-construction planning process so that we are ready to complete the remainder of the capital raise and remain on schedule. Furthermore, the additional liquidity provides us greater flexibility for other capital opportunities.” Citizens Capital Markets served as financial advisor to Bally’s , while Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson LLP served as legal advisor. Citizens Capital Markets and Fried Frank provided advisory and legal services.

stories.title: Stockdale Leads $157M Shopping Center Acquisition in Southern California
stories.excerpt: As more capital returns to brick-and-mortar retail, a Los Angeles-based investment firm has gone east to acquire a shopping center in the Inland Empire. Stockdale Capital Partners and funds managed by Conshohocken, Pa.-based Hamilton Lane put down $157 million for a 378,140-square-foot lifestyle center at 13920 City Center Drive in Chino Hills, Calif., called the Shoppes at Chino Hills. The more than 25-acre property was developed in 2008 and is anchored by Trader Joe’s and Barnes & Noble. Its tenant roster includes national retailers, restaurants and experiential concepts serving more than 300,000 residents within five miles, according to the buyers. The buyers did not disclose the occupancy rate at the property. Stockdale plans to rename the property the Shops at Chino Hills and to pursue a broader rebranding, remerchandising and repositioning program to attract more national retailers, restaurants and concepts that the buyers said are underrepresented in the market. “The Shoppes at Chino Hills represents an opportunity to acquire a true ‘Main Street’ retail environment in one of Southern California’s most desirable and supply-constrained submarkets,” Bastian Peters, who co-heads Stockdale’s retail platform with Jeff Bhathal, said in a statement. The acquisition comes as investors have become increasingly more confident in retail in general, but especially in open-air and grocery-anchored shopping centers. Hamilton Lane co-head of real estate Scott Davies said the combination of “limited supply and strong demand from both consumers and retailers” helped make the asset more attractive. Stockdale has been expanding its retail platform with a strategy focused on repositioning, lease-up and experiential upgrades. The private equity firm manages more than $3 billion across real estate sectors, including retail, multifamily, hospitality, health care and office. stories.summary: Stockdale Capital Partners and Hamilton Lane acquired the Shoppes at Chino Hills, a 378,140-square-foot lifestyle center in Chino Hills, California, for $157 million. The property, developed in 2008 and anchored by Trader Joe's and Barnes & Noble, sits on 25+ acres and serves a trade area of 300,000+ residents within five miles. The buyers plan to rebrand and remerchandise the property to attract underrepresented national retailers and experiential concepts.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. Retail acquisition and repositioning in Inland Empire does not signal residential demand or supply shifts. Indirect signal: capital returning to brick-and-mortar retail in high-density suburban trade areas (Chino Hills) may indicate stabilizing consumer spending and tax base—supportive for broader regional multifamily demand, but not a site-specific catalyst. Monitor only if retail revitalization drives employment concentration or population migration to Inland Empire submarkets.

stories.title: Essex Realty Group Markets 20-Unit Multifamily Portfolio in Chicago
stories.excerpt: Essex Realty Group, LLC has been exclusively engaged to market for sale a 20-unit portfolio, a multifamily investment opportunity comprised of five similar buildings in Chicago’s West Town neighborhood. The portfolio features 20 residential apartments, including 15 three-bedroom, two-bathroom units. Principal Jim Darrow and Director Abe Eilian represent the seller in the offering. All five properties are within walking distance of the Division CTA Blue Line Station and Division Street Corridor, with convenient access to restaurants, retail, and neighborhood amenities. The portfolio also benefits from its proximity to Fulton Market and the West Loop. “While we’ve sold portfolios with properties located relatively close to one another in the past, it’s rare to find a portfolio where all of the properties are this close together,” said Darrow. “It’s even more unusual to have buildings that are virtually identical, creating opportunities for operational efficiencies, from maintenance to rehabilitation materials, and beyond.” The conversations behind tomorrow’s apartment deals happen at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Connect with the capital sources, owners, developers, and brokers driving multifamily investment. Learn more and reserve your seat at www.connectapts2026.com. stories.summary: Essex Realty Group has been engaged to exclusively market a 20-unit multifamily portfolio comprising five similar buildings in Chicago's West Town neighborhood. The portfolio includes 15 three-bedroom, two-bathroom units plus five other units, all within walking distance of the Division CTA Blue Line Station and Division Street Corridor, with proximity to Fulton Market and West Loop dining and retail.
stories.impact: Modest supply signal for West Town/Fulton Market submarket. Sale of clustered small-buildings portfolio (five 4-unit buildings) suggests exit by mom-and-pop/legacy owner; buyer consolidation and operational efficiency play. No volume catalyst (20 units is micro-scale), but reflects market liquidity and valuation confidence in transit-rich, amenity-dense Near West Side. Developers should monitor if portfolio sells to institutional buyer—institutional ownership may trigger unit-level upgrades, rent growth, or eventual assemblage for mid-rise repositioning. Division Street corridor remains tight-supply, high-demand zone; this portfolio sale unlikely to affect rent trajectory but signals active capital circulation.

stories.title: Brazos Residential Picks Up Challenging Grand Prairie Apartment Asset
stories.excerpt: 180 Multifamily Properties sold The Watson, a 248-unit apartment community in Grand Prairie, located roughly midway between Dallas and Fort Worth. Wes Racht, Nick Fluellen, and Bard Hoover of Marcus & Millichap represented 180 Multifamily and procured the buyer, Brazos Residential. Brazos’s Wyatt Simmons added this, “The Watson was a particularly complex transaction as it required a highly structured partnership and waterfall, rescue capital, and navigating a distressed seller and property, but that complexity is exactly where we continue to find opportunity. “ The Class A property was built in 2018. Units come in one- and two-bedroom floor plans. Amenities include a pool, playground, fitness center, clubhouse and conference room, two courtyards and a bocce ball court. The property is just off Texas State Highway 360, near Interstate 30, close to the Grand Prairie Premium Outlets and Joe Pool Lake. The post Brazos Residential Picks Up Challenging Grand Prairie Apartment Asset appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Brazos Residential acquires The Watson, 248-unit Class A apartment in Grand Prairie TX

stories.summary: Brazos Residential acquired The Watson, a 248-unit Class A apartment community built in 2018 in Grand Prairie, positioned midway between Dallas and Fort Worth. The transaction was complex, requiring structured partnerships, rescue capital, and navigation of a distressed seller and property. Marcus & Millichap brokered the sale. Units include one- and two-bedroom floor plans with amenities including pool, fitness center, clubhouse, and courtyards.
stories.impact: Distressed multifamily sale in DFW secondary market signals loan stress and valuation reset. Grand Prairie (outer ring, mid-market submarket) saw heavy 2018–2022 development; The Watson's distress likely reflects overbuilding and slower lease-up post-COVID. Acquisition by value-add operator (Brazos Residential) with rescue capital indicates opportunity cost-basis, but also signals tightening leverage and higher carry costs for operators. DFW multifamily developers should underwrite Grand Prairie submarkets conservatively: 2018–2020 vintage assets face higher refi risk and cap-rate pressure. Brazos's play suggests consolidation/stabilization opportunity, but implies softer fundamentals than primary DFW core (Dallas, Plano). Monitor comparable sales to reset cost-of-capital benchmarks for DFW secondary markets.

stories.title: Hines and Rialto Credit Partners’ Debt Fund Closes at $1.1B
stories.excerpt: Real estate asset managers Hines and Rialto Capital announced Monday the final close of its office-focused credit fund Hines Rialto Credit Partners, which reached $1.1 billion in investor commitments. The co-general partnership between Hines and Rialto launched in 2024 and secured $700 million in its first close. The partners’ Monday announcement called the $1.1 billion close an indication of “investor demand for real estate credit strategies backed by specialized asset-level underwriting and deep market expertise.” “This close reflects the strength of bringing together two highly complementary platforms, and the potential opportunity we see in U.S. office credit,” Jeff Krasnoff, CEO of Rialto Capital, said in a statement. Hines Rialto Credit Partners will now focus its energies on deploying capital toward U.S. office credit investments. The fund recently supplied the $228.9 million bridge loan for the refinancing of the Textile Building at 295 Fifth Avenue by joint venture owners PGIM, Tribeca Investment Group and Meadow Partners, CO reported in July. The fund’s strategy has also included debt acquisition. In August 2025, the partners snapped up nearly $100 million in loans tied to three Midtown office buildings, The Real Deal reported. Alfonso Munk, Hines’ global co-head of investment management, said in the announcement that the rapid growth of private credit requires greater scrutiny of assets. “In real estate credit, understanding the underlying asset — what it is worth, how it performs and how it may hold up under pressure — is becoming increasingly important as the market works through a significant refinancing cycle,” Munk said. “That kind of visibility matters in any market, but particularly in a more complex credit environment.” Hines and Rialto’s shared activity thus far has spanned both coasts. The pair provided a $91 million financing package for Saca Development’s acquisition of One American Plaza in Downtown San Diego, as CO reported in October 2025,
bullets: Hines & Rialto Capital close $1.1B office-focused credit fund; first close was $700M (2024)

stories.summary: Hines and Rialto Capital announced the final close of Hines Rialto Credit Partners at $1.1 billion in investor commitments, building on a $700 million first close in 2024. The office-focused credit fund will deploy capital toward U.S. office debt investments. The fund recently originated a $228.9 million bridge loan for the Textile Building at 295 Fifth Avenue in NYC, involving joint venture owners PGIM, Tribeca Investment Group, and Meadow Partners.
stories.impact: Indirect capital signal for multifamily. Office credit fund raises and deployment signal lender appetite, but capital is earmarked for office, not residential. Macro implication: strong institutional interest in specialized real estate credit (not vanilla CMBS) suggests capital availability and pricing discipline for niche strategies. Multifamily developers should note: if similar credit funds focusing on multifamily/mixed-use were to close, it would indicate confident underwriting of residential fundamentals. Monitor Hines/Rialto's pipeline for any multifamily or mixed-use deals; currently office-focused fund does not compete directly but may signal broader capital market health.

stories.title: Dwight Investment Group Supplies $130M Refi for Phoenix Apartment Tower
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between Bridge Investment Group and Hatteras Sky has sealed $130 million of bridge debt to refinance a newly built mixed-use multifamily tower in Downtown Phoenix, Commercial Observer has learned. Dwight Investment Management provided the loan for the sponsorship’s 23-story Saiya development, completed in 2025, in a deal originated by Brandon Baksh, Tommy Ng and Talisse Thompson. In addition to repaying existing debt, the refi also funded an interest reserve, according to Dwight. “We view Saiya as a centerpiece of the broader Opportunity Zone in the area, and are excited to see it continue to flourish as retail tenants begin operations and growth across the surrounding area continues,” Baksh, managing director at Dwight,said in a statement. Located at 802 North First Avenue in Downtown Phoenix’s Roosevelt Row Arts District, the 389-unit building features apartment units ranging from studios to three-bedrooms along with 12,550 square feet of ground-floor retail space that includes a Pablo’s restaurant and wellness studio Yvree scheduled to open this fall. Resident amenities include a two-story fitness center, a rooftop lounge with a kitchen, and a dog park. Bridge Investment Group and Hatteras Sky did not immediately return a request or comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Dwight Investment Management provides $130M bridge refi for Saiya, 389-unit Phoenix multifamily tower
23-story mixed-use building completed 2025 at 802 North First Ave, Downtown Phoenix (Roosevelt Row)
Refi funds debt paydown, interest reserve; includes 12,550 sq ft ground-floor retail
stories.summary: Dwight Investment Management provided a $130 million bridge loan to refinance Saiya, a newly completed 23-story mixed-use multifamily tower in Downtown Phoenix's Roosevelt Row Arts District. The project, developed by Bridge Investment Group and Hatteras Sky, includes 389 apartment units (studios to three-bedrooms) and 12,550 square feet of ground-floor retail. The refi funded debt repayment and an interest reserve as retail tenants began operations.
stories.impact: Positive capital signal for Downtown Phoenix residential market. New-built multifamily tower (completed 2025) already refinancing suggests strong stabilization, lease-up velocity, and lender confidence in Phoenix market recovery. Bridge loan at $130M on 389 units = ~$334k/unit; indicates market rents sufficient to support bridge-level debt service. Roosevelt Row is OZ corridor with ongoing commercial/mixed-use activation (retail opening cited)—this refi signals successful lease-up and retail anchor stabilization. Developers should note: Phoenix downtown multifamily achieving bridge refinance within ~6 months of completion reflects strong demand and rent growth. Expect additional 2025–2026 completions to refinance; cap rates may compress as investors gain confidence in Phoenix rental trajectory. Track comparable refinances to benchmark Phoenix multifamily underwriting.

stories.title: J.E. Richards, Maker of Data Center Components, Signs Massive Northern Virginia Lease
stories.excerpt: A commercial electrical contractor and manufacturer based in the greater Washington, D.C., area has signed a massive industrial lease. J.E. Richards, which makes data center components, took all 935,000 square feet at Flint Development’s 211 Centreport Parkway in Stafford, Va., representing the largest industrial lease ever transacted between the Metro D.C. and D.C.-Richmond corridors, according to landlord broker JLL. J.E. Richards will have up to 500 employees working away on data center components and other hardware at the property, which is also known as Capitol 95 Logistics. The lease term is 10 years. JLL did not immediately disclose the asking rent, but the average industrial asking rent for Northern Virginia was $17.41 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a report from CBRE. JLL’s John Dettleff negotiated on behalf of Flint Development, while Michael DiMeglio and Michael Isen of NAI Michael represented J.E. Richards in the transaction. “Over the last year, we’ve seen a significant increase in large-scale industrial leasing activity across the Metro D.C. and D.C.-Richmond corridor markets, particularly for spaces of 250,000 square feet or more,” Dettleff said in a statement. “Increasingly, that demand is coming from companies supporting the data center industry, including manufacturers and other specialized users.” The NAI Michael brokers did not immediately respond to a request for comment. J.E. Richards’ lease almost matches the total square footage leased in the industrial space across the market in the second quarter. Volume in the D.C.-Richmond market reached 1 million square feet as of the end of June, which was a 55 percent increase on a year-over-year basis, according to CBRE. The transaction is the largest industrial lease ever between the Metro D.C. and D.C.-Richmond corridors. The facility will employ up to 500 workers on data center components and hardware. stories.impact: Significant indirect demand catalyst for Northern Virginia multifamily. J.E. Richards 500-employee base relocating to Stafford (outer suburban, I-95 corridor) creates workforce housing demand in underserved secondary market. Stafford is ~30 miles south of D.C. metro core; commute burden suggests multifamily developers should scout Class B/C product within 5–10 mile radius of Capitol 95 Logistics and adjacent industrial parks. Data center supply-chain manufacturing (semiconductors, components) is growth sector tied to AI infrastructure buildout—recurring hiring likely. Additionally, large industrial lease at $17.41/sf (Q2 2026) signals industrial cap rates compressing and land values rising in Stafford corridor; adjacent multifamily land values may increase. Monitor other data center–adjacent industrial/tech employment clustering in Northern Virginia; Stafford submarket may become multifamily destination play if employer density grows.
